note: Attacker-controlled CoAP POST payload is accepted as an energy-scan request and the Channel Mask TLV is parsed from it.
The TLV is copied out of the message into a fixed-size ChannelMaskTlv object before validation.
Parsing continues by walking the embedded channel-mask entries inside the copied TLV.
The loop iterates over each ChannelMaskEntry using GetNext(), which computes the next pointer from the current entry's declared size.
GetEntrySize() uses the attacker-controlled mMaskLength field, so an oversized length advances the pointer beyond the actual entry data.
The parser dereferences the ChannelMaskEntry as a full 32-bit mask even when the entry layout is shorter than expected, causing an out-of-bounds read.

code: bool IsValid(void) const { return GetMaskLength() == sizeof(mMask); }
note: The root cause is that validation only checks the mask length for exact equality, but the parser path in GetChannelMask() can still reach the sink through malformed entry chaining before a safe stop.
